Key files: packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/index.tsx, packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/\$connectorKey.index.tsx, packages/owletto/src/lib/connectors/{facets,sandbox-rows,inference-rows}.ts, packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-form.tsx, packages/server/src/lobu/client-routes.ts, packages/server/src/worker-api/{poll,device-management,device-reconcile}.ts.

Your job: find DESIGN flaws a diff-scoped code review could only catch after the code exists. Answer all 7 questions at the bottom of the doc explicitly and in order. 1	# DESIGN: collapse `/connectors/runtime` (devices) + `/connectors/apps` (MCP clients) into `/connectors`
2	
3	Status: DESIGN, not built. Repo: lobu (bun workspace, `packages/owletto` = React SPA frontend
4	submodule, `packages/server` = Hono gateway).
5	
6	## Goal
7	
8	Delete two owletto routes and fold everything they do into the single `/connectors` surface:
9	
10	- `/$owner/connectors/runtime` + `/runtime/devices/$deviceId` — "My devices" (pair a Mac /
11	  Chrome extension / CLI / Docker; list paired devices; device detail).
12	- `/$owner/connectors/apps` — "Connected apps" (MCP clients over OAuth: ChatGPT, Claude, Lobu
13	  CLI) with a Revoke button.
14	
15	User-stated intent: "put lobu cli, owletto chrome extension and owletto macos app in the
16	connectors [catalog] and just give them the instructions; when they're connected chrome
17	extension and mac show up as a connector/connection." Plus: MCP clients become rows under
18	Connectors that open a detail on click. Ship as ONE PR.
19	
20	## Substrate as it actually is (read, not assumed)
21	
22	### The connectors list is already a synthesized union
23	
24	`packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/index.tsx` builds `items` from three sources:
25	
26	1. real connector definitions (`useInstallableConnectorCatalog`) joined with connection groups
27	   (`useConnectionConnectorGroups`), filtered to `installed || connection_count > 0`;
28	2. `buildInferenceConnectorRows(inferenceProviders)` → synthetic rows keyed `inference:{slug}`;
29	3. `buildSandboxConnectorRows(sandboxes)` → synthetic rows keyed `sandbox:{id}`.
30	
31	All three render as `<Link to="/$owner/connectors/$connectorKey">`; the detail page
32	(`$connectorKey.index.tsx`, ~1300 lines) branches on the key prefix and renders
33	`InferenceProviderDetail` / `SandboxDetail` / the real connector shell. Key prefixes are
34	constants in `@lobu/core/reserved` (`SANDBOX_ROW_KEY_PREFIX`, `SANDBOX_PROVIDER_KEY_PREFIX`,
35	`INFERENCE_ROW_KEY_PREFIX`).
36	
37	Facets (`lib/connectors/facets.ts`) drive 11 filter chips: all / data / chat / actions /
38	inference / runtime / oauth / api_key / app_install / device ("On device") / needs_setup.
39	`ConnectionFacets` = `{data, chat, actions, audience, inference, runtime}`. `device` is NOT a
40	facet — it is derived via `connectorIsDeviceBound(connector)` = `!!connector.runtime ||
41	!!connector.required_capability`.
42	
43	The catalog picker (`components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-form.tsx`) composes the
44	same three families for `/connectors/create`, including
45	`buildSandboxProviderCatalogEntries(availableProviders)` → `sandbox-provider:{kind}` entries
46	whose click handler sets `selectedSandboxKind` and swaps in a locked create form — i.e. a
47	catalog entry that is NOT a connector and opens a bespoke panel is an established pattern.
48	
49	### Devices
50	
51	`device_workers` table. Registered in `packages/server/src/worker-api/poll.ts:256` — an upsert on
52	`(user_id, worker_id)` on every user-scoped worker poll. Columns used here: `user_id`,
53	`worker_id`, `platform`, `app_version`, `capabilities`, `label`, `organization_id`,
54	`connector_manifests`, `last_seen_at`. `platform` is set-once (COALESCE) as a security measure.
55	
56	`packages/core/src/capabilities.ts` `PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST` has exactly three platforms:
57	`macos`, `ios`, `chrome-extension`. A poll with any other platform (or none) gets its declared
58	capabilities dropped to `[]`. **`cli` / `node` is not a platform** — the Lobu CLI never creates a
59	`device_workers` row. The Docker bridge (`packages/connector-worker`) sends no platform, so it
60	can register a row but advertises zero capabilities.
61	
62	`GET /api/me/devices` (`worker-api/device-management.ts:40`) is **user-scoped and cross-org**:
63	`WHERE dw.user_id = ${userId}`, returning each device's `organization_id`/`organization_slug`,
64	`connector_count`, `connector_error_count`, `last_sync_at`, and the array of pinned connections.
65	`online` = `last_seen_at > now() - interval '20 minutes'`.
66	
67	Device → connectors: `worker-api/device-reconcile.ts` `reconcileDeviceCapabilities` /
68	`ensureDeviceConnectorWired` install a bundled device connector definition, a no-auth connection,
69	and the first feed into the user's org for each capability the fresh device fleet advertises, and
70	auto-pin `connections.device_worker_id` when exactly one fresh device qualifies. So a paired Mac
71	ALREADY materializes Screen Time / Photos / Calendar / Reminders / computer_use rows in the
72	connectors list today.
73	
74	Device detail route `runtime/devices/$deviceId.tsx` is 404 lines: rename (`PATCH
75	/api/me/devices/:id`), delete (`DELETE`, which tombstones device pins via
76	`utils/device-pin-tombstones.ts`), a `RunsPanel`, capability chips (`CAPABILITY_LABELS`), auth
77	profiles, and links back to pinned connections.
78	
79	### MCP clients
80	
81	`GET /api/:orgSlug/clients` (`packages/server/src/lobu/client-routes.ts:210`) returns
82	`oauth_clients` rows for the org, mapped to `ConnectedClientItem` plus messaging clients
83	(`kind: "messaging"`). `DELETE /mcp/:clientId?scope=all` revokes.
84	
85	`apps.tsx` filters to `kind === "mcp"` and groups by server-provided `registrationGroupKey`
86	(`JSON.stringify([client_name, owner_user_id, organizationId])`) because a client that
87	re-registers creates a new row under the same name. `groupClients()` is exported FROM the route
88	file and imported by `lib/group-clients.test.ts`. `kind: "messaging"` clients are fetched and
89	rendered nowhere.
90	
91	**Known identity defect (measured on prod 2026-07-30):** `client-routes.ts:258` computes
92	`title = clientInfo.name || client_name` — the per-session `initialize` clientInfo WINS over the
93	DCR registration name. Result: 5 of 19 prod rows display a different vendor than they registered
94	as — `Owletto for Mac → claude-code` (x3), `Lobu CLI → claude-code`, `Claude → claude-code`.
95	`isFirstPartyLobuClient(title, softwareId)` (`client-routes.ts:56`) therefore evaluates FALSE for
96	the real Lobu first-party clients, because `title` is "claude-code" and `software_id` is NULL on
97	all 19 prod rows. `client-session-routes.ts` joins `oauth_clients.client_name` — the opposite
98	precedence, so the two surfaces disagree.
99	
100	`metadata.last_agent_id` is NULL on all 19 prod rows, so the `agentId` filter at
101	`client-routes.ts:255` drops every client from any agent-scoped view.
102	
103	### Entry points that must be repointed (grepped, excluding routeTree.gen)
104	
105	To `/connectors/runtime` or `/runtime/devices/$deviceId`:
106	- `app/index.tsx:107` — hand-built URL string
107	- `app/$owner/connectors/$connectorKey.index.tsx:1080`, `:1241`
108	- `components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-form.tsx:781`, `:1413` ("Add device")
109	- `components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-settings-tab.tsx:450`
110	- `components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/connection-feed-detail.tsx:83`
111	- `components/devices/devices-body.tsx:47`
112	- `components/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:471` (user menu "My devices")
113	- `app/__smoke__/all-routes.test.tsx:204,205,217,218`
114	
115	To `/connectors/apps`:
116	- `components/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:485` (user menu "Connected apps")
117	- `components/home/client-sessions-timeline.tsx:63`
118	- `app/__smoke__/all-routes.test.tsx:210,211`
119	- `lib/group-clients.test.ts:2`
120	
121	## Proposed design
122	
123	### 1. Devices become `device:{id}` rows in the connectors list
124	
125	New `lib/connectors/device-rows.ts` mirroring `sandbox-rows.ts` exactly:
126	`buildDeviceConnectorRows(devices)` → `{connector, facets, device}` with
127	`connector.key = "device:{id}"`, `name = deviceName(device)`,
128	`status = device.online ? "active" : "error"`, facets `{runtime: true}` (rest false).
129	
130	Rationale for `runtime` rather than a new facet: a paired Mac is the local counterpart of a
131	remote sandbox — the sandbox lede already says sandboxes are where agents execute "instead of
132	the built-in local runtime". Sandboxes are already `runtime`-faceted rows in this list.
133	
134	Row meta line: `macOS · 5 connectors · online` / `offline 2h`.
135	`needsSetup` = false (a device with no capabilities is not "unconfigured", it is a device).
136	
137	Detail: `$connectorKey.index.tsx` gains a `device:` branch rendering a `DeviceDetail` component
138	extracted verbatim from today's `runtime/devices/$deviceId.tsx` body. Route
139	`/$owner/connectors/runtime/*` is deleted; `/$owner/connectors/device:{id}` is the new home.
140	
141	### 2. MCP clients become `client:{groupKey}` rows in the connectors list
142	
143	`buildClientConnectorRows(clientGroups)` from the existing `groupClients()` output (moved to
144	`lib/clients/group-clients.ts` so a route file stops exporting logic).
145	`connector.key = "client:{groupKey}"` — NOTE `registrationGroupKey` is a JSON array string
146	containing `"` and `,`; it must be URL-encoded into the route param and decoded back.
147	Row meta: `Burak Emre · active 3m ago` / `disconnected`.
148	
149	New facet needed: none of the six `ConnectionFacets` fit ("what an app can do for your agent" is
150	the wrong axis for an inbound client). Proposal: add a 12th filter chip `client` ("Apps") that
151	matches on the key prefix rather than on a facet, keeping `ConnectionFacets` unchanged.
152	
153	Detail: a `client:` branch in `$connectorKey.index.tsx` rendering identity (registered name,
154	driven-by clientInfo, redirect_uris host, software id/version), linked user, last seen, active
155	token count, sessions, and Revoke (admin-only, already `withOrgAdmin`-gated server-side).
156	
157	### 3. Install recipes move into the catalog
158	
159	`components/devices/device-connect.tsx` today is four stateless accordions (macOS app → "Contact
160	us" link; Chrome extension → web store link; CLI → `npm i -g @lobu/cli && lobu login && lobu
161	memory configure --url {mcpUrl}`; Docker → `docker run …`). These become catalog entries
162	`install:{id}` in the `/connectors/create` picker, using the `sandbox-provider:` mechanic: click
163	sets state and swaps in an instructions panel instead of a form.
164	
165	Same family gains MCP-client recipes (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, Codex) built from
166	`buildMcpUrl(orgSlug)` — the GUI form of what `lobu memory configure --url` does today.
167	
168	"Add device" CTAs (`connection-form.tsx:1413`, `connection-settings-tab.tsx:450`) repoint from
169	the devices LIST to `/connectors/create` filtered to these entries — i.e. they now land on
170	instructions, which is what they wanted in the first place.
171	
172	### 4. Client identity fix (server)
173	
174	`client-routes.ts`: `title` becomes `client_name` (DCR registration) with `clientInfo.name`
175	demoted to a new `drivenBy` field. `isFirstPartyLobuClient` keys off `client_name` +
176	`redirect_uris` host. This is a prerequisite for (2) and (5) — without it, the three Lobu
177	first-party surfaces all label themselves "claude-code" in prod.
178	
179	### 5. Device/client de-duplication
180	
181	The Owletto Mac app creates BOTH a `device_workers` row AND an `oauth_clients` row; there is no
182	FK between the tables. Without a rule it appears twice in the merged list. Proposed rule: a
183	first-party client row is suppressed when a `device:` row exists for the same
184	`(owner_user_id, platform)`. Depends on (4) for a trustworthy platform signal.
185	
186	### 6. Scoping (OPEN — reviewer should attack this)
187	
188	`/connectors` is org-scoped. `GET /api/me/devices` is user-scoped and cross-org. Proposed v1:
189	filter client-side to `device.organization_id === current org`. Consequence: a teammate's paired
190	Mac is invisible even though `ensureDeviceConnectorWired` may have wired its connectors into an
191	org you can see. Proper fix (deferred): an org-scoped device endpoint with owner attribution,
192	admin-only delete, owner-only rename.
193	
194	### 7. Redirects
195	
196	`/connectors/runtime` → `/connectors`; `/connectors/runtime/devices/$deviceId` →
197	`/connectors/device:{id}`; `/connectors/apps` → `/connectors`. Repo precedent exists
198	(`/environments` → `/connectors`, `memory/memory-legacy-redirects.test.tsx`). Note repo rule
199	"no backwards-compat shims" — argued as not applicable to bookmarkable user-facing URLs.
200	
201	### 8. Ship shape
202	
203	ONE PR (user's explicit instruction), covering: server identity fix + device rows + client rows +
204	two detail branches + catalog install recipes + deletion of 4 route files + 12 repointed call
205	sites + redirects + tests.
206	
207	## Questions for the reviewer
208	
209	1. Is putting an inbound MCP client (a thing that calls INTO Lobu with a person's access) in the
210	   same list as outbound connectors (things an agent reaches OUT to) a category error that will
211	   cost more than the page it saves? A prior session's adversarial review rejected exactly this
212	   for a Runtime tab and instead decided MCP clients are "external agents" belonging on the
213	   Agents page. The user has now overruled that. What breaks?
214	2. Revoking a client's grant and deleting an org connection are different danger classes on one
215	   page. Is prefix-branching the detail page enough separation, or does the LIST need it?
216	3. Is `runtime` the right facet for a device, given a device is BOTH a runtime and a source of
217	   connectors (whose provided connectors already appear as their own rows)?
218	4. Section 6 scoping: is the client-side org filter honest, or does it under-report in a way that
219	   makes the merged list wrong?
220	5. Section 5 de-dup: is suppression right, or should the two identities be linked properly?
221	6. Is ONE PR defensible here, or does the server-side identity fix (independently
222	   prod-verifiable, different blast radius, different rollback) have to be split out?
223	7. What did this design miss — specifically in `$connectorKey.index.tsx`'s existing prefix
224	   branching, the `connection_count`/`needsSetup` sort invariants, and the catalog picker's
225	   `installedOnly` mode?
226

1	import { getAuthMethods } from "@/components/entity-tabs/connections-tab/auth-methods";
2	import type {
3	  ConnectionConnectorGroup,
4	  ConnectionFacets,
5	  ConnectorDefinitionItem,
6	} from "@/lib/api/connections";
7	
8	/**
9	 * Connector capability facets + the shared filter vocabulary used by BOTH the
10	 * connectors grid (`/connectors`) and the Add-connector catalog picker. Keeping
11	 * the filter keys, labels, and matcher here means the two chip rows can never
12	 * drift — add a filter once and both pages get it.
13	 */
14	
15	/** The capability facets a connector card advertises. */
16	export type ConnectorFacet =
17	  | "data"
18	  | "chat"
19	  | "actions"
20	  | "device"
21	  | "inference"
22	  | "runtime";
23	
24	/** Every filter chip a connector list can offer. */
25	export type ConnectorFilter =
26	  | "all"
27	  | "data"
28	  | "chat"
29	  | "actions"
30	  | "inference"
31	  | "runtime"
32	  | "oauth"
33	  | "api_key"
34	  | "app_install"
35	  | "device"
36	  | "needs_setup";
37	
38	/** The canonical chip label for every filter. */
39	export const CONNECTOR_FILTER_LABELS: Record<ConnectorFilter, string> = {
40	  all: "All",
41	  data: "Data",
42	  chat: "Chat",
43	  actions: "Actions",
44	  inference: "Inference",
45	  runtime: "Runtime",
46	  oauth: "OAuth",
47	  api_key: "API key",
48	  app_install: "App install",
49	  device: "On device",
50	  needs_setup: "Needs setup",
51	};
52	
53	/**
54	 * A connector declares itself chat-capable via the `x-lobu-chat-platform`
55	 * marker in its `options_schema` (slack/telegram/discord/… all set it). This is
56	 * the DEFINITION-level signal — the same one the server reads at connect time —
57	 * so an uninstalled chat connector can advertise chat before any connection
58	 * exists. Catalog use only: per-connection `facets.chat` stays live-only (it
59	 * means "a live bot adapter", which the run-on-device picker keys off).
60	 */
61	export function connectorDeclaresChat(
62	  connector: ConnectorDefinitionItem
63	): boolean {
64	  return connector.options_schema?.["x-lobu-chat-platform"] != null;
65	}
66	
67	/** Whether a connector runs on a device (needs a local runtime to execute). */
68	export function connectorIsDeviceBound(
69	  connector: ConnectorDefinitionItem
70	): boolean {
71	  return !!connector.runtime || !!connector.required_capability;
72	}
73	
74	/**
75	 * Derive a connector's capability facets. A live connection group's facets win
76	 * (they reflect actual configured state); otherwise fall back to what the
77	 * connector definition declares, so an uninstalled connector still advertises
78	 * what it CAN do (data/chat/actions).
79	 */
80	export function deriveConnectorFacets(
81	  connector: ConnectorDefinitionItem,
82	  group?: ConnectionConnectorGroup
83	): ConnectionFacets {
84	  const feeds = connector.feeds_schema
85	    ? Object.keys(connector.feeds_schema).length > 0
86	    : false;
87	  const actions =
88	    connector.has_operations ||
89	    (connector.actions_schema
90	      ? Object.keys(connector.actions_schema).length > 0
91	      : false);
92	  return {
93	    data: group?.facets.data ?? feeds,
94	    chat: group?.facets.chat ?? connectorDeclaresChat(connector),
95	    actions: group?.facets.actions ?? actions,
96	    audience: group?.facets.audience ?? false,
97	    // A connector definition never serves inference or runtime — model
98	    // providers and sandboxes live in their own tables and are synthesized into
99	    // the list as their own rows (see the connectors index). Nothing derived
100	    // from a connector can flip either.
101	    inference: false,
102	    runtime: false,
103	  };
104	}
105	
106	/** The connector + derived state a filter is evaluated against. */
107	export interface ConnectorFilterItem {
108	  connector: ConnectorDefinitionItem;
109	  facets: ConnectionFacets;
110	  /** Installed-but-unconfigured. Optional — catalog entries have no setup state. */
111	  needsSetup?: boolean;
112	}
113	
114	/**
115	 * The single matcher both connector lists use. A filter falls into one of three
116	 * buckets: capability facet (data/chat/actions/inference/runtime/device), auth
117	 * method (oauth/api_key/app_install), or setup state (needs_setup).
118	 */
119	export function connectorMatchesFilter(
120	  item: ConnectorFilterItem,
121	  filter: ConnectorFilter
122	): boolean {
123	  const { connector, facets } = item;
124	  if (filter === "all") return true;
125	  if (filter === "data") return facets.data;
126	  if (filter === "chat") return facets.chat;
127	  if (filter === "actions") return facets.actions;
128	  if (filter === "inference") return facets.inference;
129	  if (filter === "runtime") return facets.runtime === true;
130	  if (filter === "device") return connectorIsDeviceBound(connector);
131	
132	  const methods = getAuthMethods(connector.auth_schema);
133	  if (filter === "oauth") return methods.some((m) => m.type === "oauth");
134	  if (filter === "api_key") return methods.some((m) => m.type === "env_keys");
135	  if (filter === "app_install") {
136	    return methods.some((m) => m.type === "app_installation");
137	  }
138	
139	  if (filter === "needs_setup") return item.needsSetup === true;
140	  return false;
141	}
142

1	import { INFERENCE_ROW_KEY_PREFIX } from "@lobu/core/reserved";
2	import type {
3		ConnectionFacets,
4		ConnectorDefinitionItem,
5	} from "@/lib/api/connections";
6	import type { InferenceProviderItem } from "@/lib/api/inference-providers";
7	
8	/**
9	 * Model providers as connectors-list rows.
10	 *
11	 * A provider IS something you connect with a credential that can fail and need
12	 * rotating — the same operational shape as every other connector row — so it
13	 * belongs in the connectors list rather than on a bespoke page. But it is NOT a
14	 * connection: providers live in their own `inference_providers` table, whose
15	 * DDL CHECK constraints (capabilities-key whitelist, base_url userinfo ban,
16	 * models_endpoint path whitelist, row-unique api_key_ref, …) are a deliberate
17	 * security floor that `connections` neither has nor could meaningfully enforce.
18	 * This is a READ-LAYER union only: we synthesize display rows, we do not move
19	 * any data.
20	 *
21	 * This mirrors the existing "group without a connector definition" synthesis in
22	 * the connectors index — same pattern, different source table.
23	 */
24	
25	/**
26	 * Namespace prefix for a synthesized provider row's `key`. Provider slugs and
27	 * connector keys share one map/list, so the prefix keeps a provider named e.g.
28	 * `slack` from colliding with the real Slack connector. The prefixed key IS the
29	 * routable connector key: provider rows link to `/connectors/$connectorKey`,
30	 * where the detail route strips the prefix and resolves the remainder as a
31	 * provider (or a provider-catalog kind) instead of a connector definition.
32	 *
33	 * Defined in `@lobu/core/reserved` because the server's URL builders emit the
34	 * same prefixed key into chat-message links; re-exported here so browser code
35	 * keeps one import site for provider-row concerns.
36	 */
37	export { INFERENCE_ROW_KEY_PREFIX };
38	
39	/**
40	 * The provider slug (or catalog kind) a routable connector key stands for, or
41	 * null when the key is a plain connector key. The single parse the detail
42	 * route branches on.
43	 */
44	export function parseInferenceRowKey(connectorKey: string): string | null {
45		if (!connectorKey.startsWith(INFERENCE_ROW_KEY_PREFIX)) return null;
46		const slug = connectorKey.slice(INFERENCE_ROW_KEY_PREFIX.length);
47		return slug.length > 0 ? slug : null;
48	}
49	
50	/** A connectors-list row synthesized from an `inference_providers` row. */
51	export interface InferenceConnectorRow {
52		connector: ConnectorDefinitionItem;
53		facets: ConnectionFacets;
54		/** The provider this row stands for — drives the row's link target. */
55		provider: InferenceProviderItem;
56	}
57	
58	/**
59	 * Turn the org's model providers into connectors-list rows. `installed: true`
60	 * because an `inference_providers` row only exists once the org added it — the
61	 * same "it's in your workspace" meaning the list filters on.
62	 */
63	export function buildInferenceConnectorRows(
64		providers: readonly InferenceProviderItem[],
65	): InferenceConnectorRow[] {
66		return providers.map((provider) => ({
67			provider,
68			facets: {
69				data: false,
70				chat: false,
71				actions: false,
72				audience: false,
73				inference: true,
74				runtime: false,
75			},
76			connector: {
77				key: `${INFERENCE_ROW_KEY_PREFIX}${provider.slug}`,
78				name: provider.displayName || provider.slug,
79				description: null,
80				version: "",
81				auth_schema: null,
82				feeds_schema: null,
83				actions_schema: null,
84				options_schema: null,
85				// The provider's own lifecycle state, so the row can show it the way
86				// every other connector row shows its state.
87				status: provider.status,
88				login_enabled: false,
89				installed: true,
90			} as ConnectorDefinitionItem,
91		}));
92	}
93

All substrate verification is done — I read every file the doc cites, and its factual claims are largely accurate (one exception noted below). Here is the adversarial design review.

---

## Verdict up front

The device half of this merge is sound and follows a real, proven pattern (sandbox rows). The MCP-client half contains one flaw that will not work as specified (the §5 dedup join key does not exist in the data), one that is actively dangerous (suppression hides live OAuth grants behind a spoofable text identity), and one that is physically impossible as written (§8's ONE PR — `packages/owletto` is a git submodule of a separate repo, confirmed in `.gitmodules`, so the server fix and the UI change cannot be one PR under any circumstances). None of these kill the project; all of them must change before code is written.

First, substrate corrections — the doc claims it read everything, and it mostly did, but: `$connectorKey.index.tsx` is 2,121 lines, not ~1300. `groupClients()` is exported from `packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/apps.tsx:43`, not from the server route file (the doc's phrasing "exported FROM the route file" is right only if "route file" means the owletto route — worth being precise since the move target differs). And the claim "the Lobu CLI never creates a `device_workers` row" has the right conclusion but the wrong mechanism: `PLATFORM_ALLOWLIST` (`capabilities.ts:56`) governs *capabilities*, not row creation — `poll.ts:255` upserts a row for **any** user-scoped worker regardless of platform, and `poll.ts:120` even re-anchors anonymous local polls into device rows. The CLI creates no row because it never polls `/api/workers/poll`, not because of the allowlist. This matters for the design: Docker bridges and any future `lobu run`-style worker **will** produce `device:{id}` rows with `platform: null`, rendering as "Device" (`device-display.tsx:36`) with zero capabilities — the row builder must handle them, and the doc's "macOS · 5 connectors" meta line is the happy path only.

## Q1 — Is inbound-client-in-the-connectors-list a category error?

Split verdict. **Devices: not a category error.** A paired Mac is an org-side capability holder that runs agents (it has a RunsPanel, it's the pin target of the run-on-device picker) — it is genuinely the local sibling of a `sandbox:` row, and the synthesis pattern (`sandbox-rows.ts`) transplants cleanly.

**MCP clients: yes, it is a category error, and the design's own text proves it.** Every existing row in this list participates in one type system: the six `ConnectionFacets` axes answer "what can this do *for* your agents." The design admits no facet fits and proposes a chip that matches on key prefix instead of on a facet (§2) — that is the tell that the row type doesn't belong to the page's ontology, it's bolted on. What concretely breaks:

1. **Direction confusion with real money attached.** The list will contain an "OpenAI" inference-provider row (outbound, your API key) and can simultaneously contain a "ChatGPT" client row (inbound, a member's grant). Both render identically as `<Link>` rows with an icon and a meta line. A user who wants to *connect ChatGPT as a tool* will click the client row; a user auditing *who has access* will read the provider row. Today the apps page's lede (`apps.tsx:109` — "They authenticate as a person and act with that person's access") does the disambiguation; the merge deletes that sentence's home.
2. **Untrusted display names enter a trusted list.** `client_name` is set via unauthenticated Dynamic Client Registration. Today those names are quarantined on a page labeled as inbound apps. Merged and alphabetically sorted (`index.tsx:302` is a flat `localeCompare` interleave), a client that registered as "GitHub" sits next to — or instead of — the real GitHub connector. It takes a member actually completing an OAuth grant to appear, so this is misleading rather than trivially exploitable, but the list stops being a trustworthy inventory.
3. **Per-viewer content** (detailed under Q4) — client rows are org-visible, device rows are viewer-private, so the merged "org connectors list" renders differently for every member. The page stops being a shared artifact two people can discuss.

The user has overruled the prior "external agents" verdict, so ship it — but as a **labeled section** ("Connected apps", pinned below the connector/provider/sandbox rows, carrying the old lede as its section subtitle), never as interleaved rows in the flat sort. That preserves the single-page goal while keeping the ontologies visually distinct. If interleaving is non-negotiable, this reviewer's position is that the page it saves costs more than it's worth.

## Q2 — Revoke vs delete: is prefix-branching the detail enough?

For the **detail** page, yes: the server already enforces the right boundaries independently (`withOrgAdmin` on the revoke at `client-routes.ts:323`; `user_id = caller` ownership on device delete at `device-management.ts:544`), so a UI branch cannot escalate anything. For the **list**, the separation needed is the sectioning from Q1, not a safety mechanism — no destructive action lives on list rows.

But there is a danger-class problem the question doesn't name: **device delete is a cross-org action that the merge relocates into an org-scoped page.** `deleteDeviceWorker` unpins and pauses connections in *every* workspace (`device-management.ts:528-535` has no org predicate; the current UI even says "across every workspace", `$deviceId.tsx:289`). Today that button lives under a user-scoped "My devices" surface where cross-org blast radius is coherent. Inside `/acme/connectors/device:{id}`, a user will reasonably believe "Remove device" removes it *from acme*. The design must either keep the "every workspace" copy prominent or (better) offer "unpin from this workspace" (which is just `PATCH` semantics) as the org-scoped action, with full removal clearly marked as global.

## Q3 — Is `runtime` the right facet for a device?

Defensible but insufficient, and the design walks into a vocabulary trap it half-noticed. The `device` chip ("On device") matches via `connectorIsDeviceBound(connector)` (`facets.ts:130` → `!!connector.runtime || !!connector.required_capability`), and a synthesized device row built "mirroring sandbox-rows exactly" has neither field. Result: **clicking "On device" shows Screen Time and Photos but not a single actual device**, while devices hide under "Runtime" next to Vercel sandboxes. Users will not recover that mapping. Fix at design level: device rows must match *both* chips — special-case the `device:` prefix in `connectorMatchesFilter`, exactly the mechanism §2 already proposes for the client chip. Second issue: `status = online ? "active" : "error"` copies the sandbox convention, but sandbox `error` means a genuine fault (missing credential), while a device that's offline is usually a lid-closed laptop. Rendering routine sleep as an error state trains users to ignore red. Use a third state or plain "offline" text; don't overload `error`.

## Q4 — Is the client-side org filter honest?

No — it under-reports in three distinct ways, and the design only names one of them:

1. **Teammates' devices invisible while their consequences are visible** (the doc's own admission): the org list shows "Screen Time — 1 connection" rows wired by `ensureDeviceConnectorWired` from a teammate's Mac, with no device row explaining where they run.
2. **Your own device disappears from the org where it matters.** Devices home to the personal org (`mint-child-token` binds there explicitly, `device-management.ts:226-233`; poll COALESCEs to personal org, `poll.ts:260-263`). Pin its connections into a team org and the team org's `/connectors` — the page you actually work in — filters the device row out (`organization_id !== currentOrg`), while `/connectors/device:{id}` still resolves (it reads unfiltered `useDevices()`). Row absent, detail reachable, breadcrumb pointing at a list that doesn't contain it.
3. **Admins get no fleet view at all**, which was at least honest when the page was called "My devices" and stops being honest when the page is the org's connector inventory.

There is a strictly better v1 filter available with **zero server work**, which the design missed: `GET /api/me/devices` already returns each pinned connection's `organization_slug` per device (`device-management.ts:75`). Filter to `device.organization_id === org || device.connectors.some(c => c.organization_slug === org)` — a device appears wherever it is *relevant*, which fixes failure 2 outright. Failures 1 and 3 genuinely need the deferred org-scoped endpoint; deferring is fine, but the page copy must say "your devices" on the section header so the under-report is labeled, not silent.

## Q5 — Suppression or linkage?

Suppression is wrong three times over; this is the strongest finding in the review.

1. **The join key does not exist.** The rule is "suppress a first-party client row when a `device:` row exists for the same `(owner_user_id, platform)`." The client row's `platform` field is `software_id` (`client-routes.ts:275`) — NULL on all 19 prod rows by the doc's own measurement, and §4 does not change that: §4 fixes *title* precedence; `software_id` is client-asserted DCR metadata that nothing backfills. So the rule as specified evaluates to "never suppress" in prod, and any fallback becomes matching `client_name` text ("Owletto for Mac" → macos) — the exact text-matcher-as-boundary anti-pattern.
2. **Suppression hides a live credential.** There is no FK between the tables; deleting a device row revokes device PATs at best, never the client's OAuth tokens. The suppressed row *is* the revocation surface, and §8 deletes `apps.tsx`, so a suppressed grant is invisible **everywhere**. Concretely: user deletes their Mac's device row believing access is gone; the "Owletto for Mac" client row pops back into the list with tokens that were live the entire time — or worse, the inverse: while the device row exists, an attacker-registered DCR client named "Owletto for Mac" (names are unauthenticated; `isFirstPartyLobuClient`'s own comment at `client-routes.ts:49-55` says "could in theory be spoofed — this is a display category, not an access boundary") is suppressed from the only page where an admin could see and revoke it. §5 silently promotes a self-declared display category into an access-visibility boundary.
3. **Suppression is viewer-relative**, because it depends on `/api/me/devices`: the Mac's owner doesn't see the client row, every other member does. Same org, same page, different app inventories.

Link, don't suppress. Real linkage means the server stamps the association at the only moment it actually knows both sides — the device-authorization grant / child-token mint, where the flow holds the OAuth `client_id` and the `worker_id` simultaneously — as a column, not a heuristic. Until that column exists, show both rows and cross-reference them textually on their detail pages ("This device also holds an MCP grant → row"). Also note §4's replacement first-party signal, `redirect_uris` host, is weak: loopback redirect URIs are what *every* local tool registers, including claude-code itself. Fine for display grouping; never for suppression or trust.

## Q6 — Is ONE PR defensible?

It is not merely undefensible — it is **impossible**. `packages/owletto` is a git submodule (`.gitmodules`: `url = https://github.com/lobu-ai/owletto.git`, gitlink mode 160000). The §4 server fix lives in the lobu repo; §§1-3/7 live in the owletto repo. The floor is two PRs in two repos, owletto merged first, then the lobu PR carrying the submodule pointer bump. Given that floor, split §4 out as its own lobu PR anyway: it has a measured prod defect as its reproducer (5/19 rows mislabeled), it is red→green testable against `/api/:orgSlug/clients`, it is prod-verifiable within minutes of rollout, and bundling it with the pointer bump means a UI regression rollback also rolls back a correctness fix that three surfaces depend on. Recommended shape: (a) lobu PR — §4 identity fix; (b) owletto PR — everything client-side; (c) lobu PR — pointer bump + redirect-adjacent server pieces if any. This should be surfaced to the user as a constraint discovered, not silently reinterpreted. One more §7 note: the doc cites "/environments → /connectors" as redirect precedent, but `reserved.ts:49-52` records that those redirect shims were **deleted** on 2026-07-28 and old links now 404 — the live precedent (memory legacy redirects) supports doing it, the cited one argues it's temporary scaffolding. Fine either way, but cite the right precedent and note that old `/connectors/runtime` bookmarks will otherwise fall through to `$connectorKey` with `connectorKey="runtime"` and render the "not installed" dead end.

## Q7 — What the design missed

In the three areas the question names, plus what fell out of verification:

**`$connectorKey.index.tsx` prefix branching.** (a) The route *loader* (lines 139-168) guards its connector-defs/connections prefetch on exactly the three known prefixes; `device:`/`client:` keys will fall through and fire `useConnections(orgId, { connectorKey: "device:…" })` prefetches — wasted queries, and a trap for whoever adds server-side handling later. Every new prefix touches the loader, the branch ladder, and the list/meta plumbing; budget for that, don't "mirror sandbox-rows exactly." (b) The prefixes belong in `@lobu/core/reserved` per the established convention (`reserved.ts:126-155` exists precisely to stop an installable custom connector — which can carry an arbitrary key — from colliding with a synthesized row's namespace); the design puts `device-rows.ts` in owletto's lib with no reservation. (c) "Extracted verbatim" contradicts the shell contract: the sandbox and provider branches were deliberately rebuilt inside `ConnectorPageShell` with the full `CONNECTOR_TABS` bar ("Tabs are never hidden…", lines 801-811), while `$deviceId.tsx` has its own page chrome (own h1, RunsPanel grid, no tabs). Verbatim extraction produces the one detail branch that looks nothing like its siblings; the design must specify the tab mapping (Overview = runs? Settings = rename/delete/browser profiles?) — that's a design decision, not a mechanical move. (d) `client:{groupKey}` as a path param is worse than the doc's "must be URL-encoded" caveat admits: `registrationGroupKey` embeds `client_name`, an unauthenticated attacker-controlled string that may contain `/` (an encoded `%2F` in a path segment is exactly the thing proxies and normalizers mangle), and the key is *unstable* — it changes when a client re-registers under a different name, breaking bookmarks. Route on `client_id` (stable, server-issued, URL-safe) and resolve the group from it on the detail page.

**`connection_count` / `needsSetup` / sort invariants.** The flat sort (needsSetup first, then `localeCompare`) interleaves three ontologies and, per Q1, puts DCR-supplied names into the alphabet next to real connectors — sectioning fixes this. `needsSetup: false` for devices is right; but note the empty-catalog auto-redirect (`index.tsx:316-326`): once client/device rows count as items, a fresh org whose only "item" is one connected MCP client no longer bounces to `/connectors/create` — it lands on a one-row list of an inbound grant. Exclude synthesized client rows from the `emptyCatalog` predicate. Also the entity-scoped view (`entityId != null`) explicitly zeroes providers/sandboxes (lines 129-132); device/client rows need the same exclusion or they'll appear inside "connectors linked to one entity."

**Catalog picker `installedOnly`.** Provider and sandbox synthesized rows are hidden when `installedOnly` is on (lines 1039, 1061); the new `install:{id}` recipe entries must join that guard or the "Installed" checkbox will show never-installable instruction cards. Bigger: §3's repointed CTAs promise `/connectors/create` "filtered to these entries," but `catalogFilter` and `installedOnly` are **component state, not URL search params** — there is no deep-linkable filter today. That's new search-param plumbing the design doesn't budget, and without it the "Add device" CTA lands on the full catalog with the recipes buried alphabetically.

**Unclaimed leftovers.** `kind: "messaging"` clients remain fetched-and-rendered-nowhere after the merge — the design carries the dead weight forward without deciding. `useConnectedClients` brings a 60-second `refetchInterval` (`apps.tsx:98`) onto the main connectors page for every viewer — drop or lengthen it. And the doc's own §1 meta line needs a decision for platform-null rows (Docker bridges) per the substrate correction above.
